about: The interim register of the engine seam (geom_op::engine::Engine, which programs reach through engine-geometry): one row for each operation of the trait and each case of its inputs that a different part answers, saying what answers it today in geom-solidcore's engine (SolidcoreEngine), the test of tests/engine.rs that pins today's answer, its known faults (ids of tests/named-faults.json), the tolerance it works to, and the kernel piece or chapter that will make it exact. Where the kernel's own exact operation answers a case, it does; solidcore answers only what the kernel cannot yet. case and answered_by are word for word what the engine's edition says. tests/engine.rs fails while an operation of the trait has no row here, a row names a test or fault that does not exist, or the edition answers otherwise. Every lane that adds an operation to the trait, or moves a case to another engine, adds or changes its row here.

operations.answered_by: geom-solidcore's own record: the engine's name, solidcore's repository and pinned commit, the grid step, solidcore's default tolerances and the answers below
operations.tolerance: none: it reports, it does not compute
operations.exact_by: stays: an exact engine of the kernel's own gives its own edition (chapter 26, versions and editions)

operations.case: a profile with no holes, level, swept straight up, which make.prism takes (strictly convex)
operations.tolerance: exact: the kernel's own prism on the grid

operations.case: every other profile: holes, a profile not level or not swept straight up, or one make.prism refuses
operations.tolerance: solidcore's zone of 1e-5 m (0.01 mm); the body is converted to the grid, each flat face's plane written through its own grid corners, recorded Certified within that and a step, and checked by geom-check at its full level
operations.exact_by: geom-sweep's Extrude (chapter 13.4) on the kernel's exact grid; until then a profile with a round hole stays refused (SC-8)

operations.tolerance: exact: the arrangement of flat faces adds no error, and the result is as exact as the least exact operand
operations.exact_by: already the kernel's exact geom-bool (chapter 11); curved operands wait for chapter 11's certified curved booleans

operations.case: sections whose walls are flat: each wall's four corners on one plane
operations.answered_by: solidcore's skin of degree 1 through the sections (create_skin_primitive)
operations.tolerance: solidcore's zone of 1e-5 m (0.01 mm); the skin's straight B-spline edges are read as the lines they are within solidcore's tolerance of each edge, the body converted to the grid, each flat face's plane written through its own grid corners, recorded Certified within that and a step, and checked by geom-check at its full level
operations.recorded: solidcore has no check that a skin does not fold back: it skins a folded section order and its own validity check passes it (lib.rs, solidcore_skins_a_folded_order_without_complaint), so geom-solidcore refuses a section not wholly ahead of the one before it as an invalid input before solidcore is reached (a_loft_that_folds_back_is_a_fault_not_a_solid). A loft whose walls cross (a section half a turn round) is refused today by solidcore's own pointer check (a_crossed_loft_is_refused_by_solidcore_s_own_check). A wall that is not flat is unsupported (a_loft_wall_that_is_not_flat_is_unsupported): the kernel has no kind for a ruled surface yet. Sections of different corner counts are refused: the caller pairs the corners, and solidcore's own matching (sweep::loft_sections) is not used, since it adds corners on no grid. A loft of three or more sections whose walls bend between sections by less than solidcore's angle tolerance (0.5 degrees) is refused today, 'the result holds a spline curve': solidcore writes the edge across those sections as one bent B-spline, which the kernel has no kind for (a_loft_whose_walls_bend_less_than_half_a_degree_is_refused; a replay of a real site's envelope found it for every loft of more than two stations over its ground). Two sections at a time loft unless a section's own sides turn by less than that tolerance: then the two walls are joined into one face whose edge is a bent B-spline, refused the same way (a_section_whose_sides_turn_less_than_half_a_degree_is_refused); sides exactly in line loft
operations.exact_by: geom-sweep's ruled loft (chapter 13.6): one face per matched edge pair, a plane where its four corners are coplanar by an exact orient3d test, so the loft is Exact; ruled faces otherwise, Certified

operations.tolerance: exact: the arrangement of flat faces adds no error, and the result's bound is the operands' combined
operations.recorded: no retry, heal or nudge. Two strips sharing a face exactly unite into one solid with the face count of the whole strip. At slivers of 0.5, 1 and 3 mm (the second strip raised by the sliver, overlapping by it, or apart by it) every union is a closed body of the closed form's volume: one shell when raised or overlapping, two shells when apart, the gap kept exactly as wide (the_sliver_unions_are_as_recorded)

operations.case: a solid with a curved face, united with one solidcore made (it keeps solidcore's body of it)
operations.tolerance: solidcore's zone of 1e-5 m (0.01 mm), merging faces closer than it (SC-1's cause); the result converted and checked by geom-check at its full level
operations.recorded: a cylinder standing on a swept box is united by solidcore and the result refused by the kernel's checker, which has no certified test yet of the pairs the circle's arcs make (engine.rs module test a_curved_solid_is_united_by_solidcore); a curved solid with one solidcore holds no body of (made by the kernel's prism or geom-bool) is unsupported (a_curved_solid_with_a_kernel_made_one_is_unsupported). No solid the seam makes today has a curved face: extrude takes polygons and loft refuses walls that are not flat
operations.exact_by: chapter 11's certified curved booleans (geom-bool), after geom-check's certified tests of arcs (CK-3)

operations.tolerance: exact for the body's rows (six times the volume in cubic steps); the body itself carries its exactness
operations.exact_by: already the kernel's (geom-topo query.volume); curved bodies wait for certified mass properties (geom-topo mass, chapter 19.2)

operations.answered_by: solidcore-tess's planar triangulation of each flat face
operations.tolerance: none on flat faces: every vertex is a corner of the body, so the mesh lies on it (delta 0, chapter 19.3); curved faces are refused as unsupported
operations.exact_by: geom-mesh's watertight tessellation and DisplayMesh (chapters 19.3 and 19.4); curved faces through solidcore-tess's planner meanwhile
